page: Amazon Web Services i8g.metal-48xl is a bare-metal storage-optimized server powered by 192 physical ARMv9 cores using the AWS Graviton Neoverse-V2 architecture running at 2.8 GHz. The system features dedicated CPU allocation with one thread per core and includes 64 KB L1d cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and 36 MB L3 cache. It is equipped with 1536 GB of DDR5 memory, providing 8 GB of RAM per physical core, alongside 45,000 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and 100 Gbps of baseline network bandwidth.

In benchmark evaluations, the instance exhibits top-tier multi-core performance, recording 295,153.48 in multi-core stress-ng tests and strong multi-core Geekbench results. Memory bandwidth reaches 871.74 GB/sec for large block reads and 403.47 GB/sec for large block writes. The bare-metal design excels in database and caching workloads, achieving 347.98 million Redis SET operations per second, top-tier database operation scores in PassMark, and 160.54 GB/sec static web serving throughput. Single-core CPU benchmarks and LLM text generation rates reflect standard general-purpose levels without specialized accelerator support.

From a resource efficiency perspective, combining 45 TB of high-speed local NVMe SSD storage with 1.5 TB of DDR5 memory minimizes external network storage overhead for latency-sensitive applications. The key tradeoff is the absence of discrete GPUs and specialized x86 vector extensions, which limits suitability for complex AI training. This instance is structured for enterprise relational databases, large-scale Redis caching clusters, software compilation, and data-intensive analytical processing.
description: Amazon Web Services i8g.metal-48xl is a bare-metal, storage-optimized instance equipped with 192 dedicated AWS Graviton Neoverse-V2 ARMv9 physical cores running at 2.8 GHz. Built for intensive memory and I/O tasks, it delivers 1536 GB of DDR5 memory, 45,000 GB of local NVMe SSD storage, and 100 Gbps baseline network throughput. Benchmark results show top-tier multi-core performance, recording 347.98 million Redis SET operations per second, 871.74 GB/sec read memory bandwidth, and high database operation scores. While single-threaded CPU benchmarks reflect standard execution speeds, its massive local SSD capacity and high memory allocation offer exceptional resource density. This server is structured for enterprise database clusters, in-memory key-value stores, large software build environments, and high-throughput web infrastructure.
